review.summary: The PR implements the analytics dashboard but breaks a large number of the spec's acceptance criteria on the server side. The visible diff (client hunks are not shown) contains 17 broken ACs — including security-relevant ones (visitor key/referrer taken from the request body, tokens logged, no admin role check, CSV formula injection, missing rate limit) — plus two changes the spec explicitly lists as out of scope. Verdict: request_changes.

findings.title: AC-1.2: analytics endpoints have no role === 'admin' check — any valid JWT passes
findings.rationale: adminRoutes.js:23 mounts the new analyticsRouter under the shared `auth` middleware only. No role-check middleware is added anywhere in the diff (analyticsRoutes.js has only query validators), and the same `auth` also guards author-facing blog routes (AC-6.6 implies an `author` role exists). A valid token with any role other than admin therefore receives 200 instead of the required 403 on every /api/admin/analytics/* endpoint.
findings.suggestion: Add a requireRole('admin') middleware (403 otherwise) inside analyticsRoutes.js or before mounting it.

findings.title: AC-2.1: period filter is applied to post createdAt, so activity on older posts is excluded (also breaks AC-2.5, AC-3.1, AC-3.4, AC-4.1, AC-4.2, AC-4.3, AC-3.7)
findings.rationale: buildBlogFilter (analyticsAggregations.js:63-72) restricts blogs to `createdAt: { $gte: from, $lte: to }`, and every analytics controller then counts views/comments only for those blogIds (views-over-time analyticsController.js:161-168, views-by-category :317-324, top-viewed :362-369, top-commented :428-439, comment-activity :277-289, last-comments :506-513, drill-down :600-609; the KPI endpoint follows the same pattern — see the prev-period mirror at :88-95). AC-2.1 requires Total Views to count BlogView documents in the selected period — scoped by view date, not post creation. With the default 30-day period, all views/comments on posts created earlier are invisible across KPIs, charts and tables.
findings.suggestion: Select blogIds by category only (plus explicit creation scoping solely for the Total Blogs card), and scope views/comments by their own timestamps.

findings.title: AC-2.4: Avg Engagement is views per published post, not comments per published post
findings.rationale: `avgEngagementCur = publishedCount > 0 ? totalViewsCur / publishedCount : 0` divides the Total Views value (line 122 uses the same variable) by the published-post count. AC-2.4 requires the average number of comments per published post; the comment totals are already computed (lines 74-87) but are not used here.
findings.suggestion: Divide the period's comment count for the selected blogs by the published-post count.

findings.title: AC-2.6: Most Active Category is the category with the most posts created, not the most views
findings.rationale: Lines 109-114 aggregate the `blogs` collection (`$group: { _id: '$category', count: { $sum: 1 } }`) over buildBlogFilter, i.e. they count posts created in the period. AC-2.6 requires the category with the most non-admin views in the period, which needs a BlogView aggregation joined to post category (as getViewsByCategory does).
findings.suggestion: Aggregate BlogView (isAdminView: false, viewedAt in period) joined to blog category.

findings.title: AC-3.5: Views by category is sorted ascending; spec requires highest→lowest from the API
findings.rationale: `{ $sort: { views: 1 } }` returns lowest-first. AC-3.5: "sorted from highest to lowest views. The order shall come from the API response (the client shall not re-sort)."

findings.title: AC-4.3: recent-comment excerpt is not stripped of HTML
findings.rationale: `contentExcerpt` is sliced from the raw `content` with no tag stripping (the 100-char slice satisfies the ≤120 bound, but the plain-text requirement is not met). AC-4.3: "a plain-text excerpt of at most 120 characters (HTML tags stripped, never rendered as HTML)". A comment containing markup is returned verbatim to the client.
findings.suggestion: Strip HTML tags server-side before slicing (e.g. reuse the client's stripHtmlTags logic or a sanitizer).

findings.title: AC-5.4: custom-range `to` date is not inclusive of the full day
findings.rationale: `parseDate` (line 13) builds `new Date(str + 'T00:00:00.000Z')`, so `to` is midnight UTC of that calendar day, and every filter uses `viewedAt/createdAt: { $lte: to }`. AC-5.4: "views recorded at any time on that calendar day (UTC) shall be counted" — everything after 00:00 UTC on the `to` day is excluded.
findings.suggestion: Set `to` to 23:59:59.999 UTC of the `to` day (as parseChartDateToRange already does for drill-down days).

findings.title: AC-5.6: CSV export does not neutralize formula-injection characters (=, +, -, @)
findings.rationale: escapeCSV only quotes cells containing commas/quotes/newlines. AC-5.6 also requires any cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` to be prefixed with a single quote. A post titled `=HYPERLINK(...)` is exported raw and will be evaluated by spreadsheet applications.
findings.suggestion: Prefix a single quote when the cell's first character is one of =, +, -, @.

findings.title: AC-6.3: visitor key is taken from the request body instead of being derived on the server
findings.rationale: `const visitorKey = req.body?.visitorKey` (line 655) is validated and stored verbatim (line 720). AC-6.3: the key shall be derived on the server as sha256(ip + user-agent) or sha256(X-Visitor-ID), and "The request body shall not be able to set the visitor key." This same PR even adds the compliant helper `computeVisitorKey` (server/src/utils/viewTracking.js:42-52), but the route wires the body-based controller instead — any client can forge keys to inflate views or evade dedup.
findings.suggestion: Use computeVisitorKey(req) from utils/viewTracking.js and ignore req.body.visitorKey.

findings.title: AC-6.4: referrer source is taken from the request body, not classified from the Referer header
findings.rationale: `const referrerSource = req.body?.referrerSource ?? 'direct'` (line 656). AC-6.4 requires server-side classification from the `Referer` header. The compliant `classifyReferrer` (server/src/utils/viewTracking.js:16-35) is added in this same PR but is not used by the route.

findings.title: AC-6.5: deduplication surfaces as a 400 error instead of a silent 200
findings.rationale: When a view from the same visitor key exists within 24h, the endpoint returns `sendError(res, VIEW_ALREADY_RECORDED, HTTP_STATUS.BAD_REQUEST)`. AC-6.5: the endpoint shall respond `200` without creating a document, and "Deduplication shall never surface as an error to the client." Every repeat page load within 24h gets an error response.
findings.suggestion: Return sendData(res, ...) (200) on the dedup path.

findings.title: AC-6.6: views by `author`-role JWTs are not marked isAdminView
findings.rationale: Only `decoded?.role === 'admin'` sets isAdminView = true. AC-6.6: a valid JWT with role `admin` **or** `author` shall be stored with isAdminView: true and excluded from all statistics. Author views are currently counted as public views.

findings.title: AC-6.7: the view endpoint has no rate limit (30 req/min per IP required)
findings.rationale: `blogRouter.post('/:blogId/view', recordView)` is registered with no limiter, and the diff adds no view limiter to rateLimiter.js (head version contains only login/comment/generate/api limiters). AC-6.7's dedicated 30-requests-per-minute-per-IP limit is never implemented.
findings.suggestion: Add a viewLimiter (windowMs: 60s, max: 30) and apply it to this route.

findings.title: AC-6.7 / out of scope: global API rate limit changed from 100 to 300 req/min
findings.rationale: The diff changes apiLimiter `max` from 100 to 300. AC-6.7: "The existing global API limit (100 req/min) shall remain unchanged", and §11 explicitly lists "Changes to global rate limits, CORS or security middleware" as out of scope for this PR.
findings.suggestion: Revert apiLimiter to max: 100; if the dashboard needs more headroom, address it via the per-endpoint limits the spec defines.

findings.title: AC-6.8: unpublished posts return 400 instead of 404
findings.rationale: `if (!blog.isPublished) return sendError(res, BLOG_NOT_PUBLISHED, HTTP_STATUS.BAD_REQUEST)`. AC-6.8: "unpublished or unknown posts return `404`" (unknown posts do return 404 at line 676).
findings.suggestion: Return HTTP_STATUS.NOT_FOUND for unpublished posts as well.

findings.title: AC-10.2: Authorization header (bearer token) written to logs
findings.rationale: `console.log('[analytics] auth header:', req.headers.authorization)` logs the raw Authorization header on every view request that carries one. AC-10.2: "Authorization headers and tokens shall never be written to logs."
findings.suggestion: Remove the console.log (the jwt.verify result is all that is needed).

findings.title: AC-10.4: CSV export issues two queries per post (unbounded, not aggregations)
findings.rationale: exportCsv loops over all matching blogs and awaits `BlogView.countDocuments` + `Comment.countDocuments` per post. AC-10.4: "Each analytics endpoint shall issue a bounded number of database queries independent of the number of posts (aggregations, not per-post queries)."
findings.suggestion: Replace the loop with two grouped aggregations (views and comment counts per blog) and merge in memory.

findings.title: Out of scope: free-text search/filtering added to the top-viewed endpoint
findings.rationale: getTopViewed accepts a `search` query param and filters titles by raw regex (`blogFilter.title = { $regex: req.query.search, $options: 'i' }`). §11 lists "Search / free-text filtering of posts" as out of scope for this PR. (The unsanitized regex is also an error/ReDoS vector.)
findings.suggestion: Remove the search parameter from this PR.

findings.title: Out of scope: changes to the existing admin Dashboard page (Written/Published This Month cards)
findings.rationale: §11 explicitly lists "Changes to the existing admin Dashboard page" as out of scope. The PR description states it "Added 'Written This Month' and 'Published This Month' statistics to the admin dashboard", and the head files confirm the new cards (Dashboard.jsx getStatCards, useAdminDashboard.js defaultDashboard, adminController.js getDashboard monthly counts). These hunks fall in the portion of the diff not shown above, so no diff line can be cited.
findings.suggestion: Move the dashboard monthly-stat changes to a separate PR or drop them from this one.
